2027-06-11.title: Saint Barnabas, Apostle
readings: for he was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith
The Lord has revealed to the nations his saving power
You received without payment; give without payment
2027-06-11.alt: Memorial. The first reading is proper to the memorial and replaces the weekday reading (2 Corinthians 4:7–15). The Gospel given is the proper Gospel of the memorial, Matthew 10:7–13; some ordos give the weekday Gospel of Friday of the Tenth Week, Matthew 5:27–32, which may also be used. Barnabas was not one of the Twelve, but the Acts of the Apostles calls him an apostle (Acts 14:14). Liturgical colour: red.
2027-06-11.verse: for he was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith. And a great many people were brought to the Lord.
theo: The Acts of the Apostles first introduces Barnabas as a generous man: a Levite from Cyprus named Joseph, “to whom the apostles gave the name Barnabas (which means ‘son of encouragement’),” who sold a field and laid the money at the apostles' feet (Acts 4:36–37). The name fits him perfectly. When Saul, the former persecutor, came to Jerusalem and the disciples were all afraid of him, it was Barnabas who “took him, brought him to the apostles,” and vouched for him (Acts 9:27). Today's reading shows him at his best. After the persecution that followed Stephen's death, believers from Cyprus and Cyrene went to Antioch, the great city of Syria, and began to preach the Lord Jesus to Greeks as well as Jews. “The hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number became believers and turned to the Lord.” The church in Jerusalem sent Barnabas to look into this new thing. He did not come with suspicion or a list of rules: “When he came and saw the grace of God, he rejoiced, and he exhorted them all to remain faithful to the Lord with steadfast devotion; for he was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith.” Then, seeing that the work was too big for him, he did something humble and wise: “Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul, and when he had found him, he brought him to Antioch.” For a whole year the two taught together, “and it was in Antioch that the disciples were first called ‘Christians.’” The second part of the reading shows the Church of Antioch at prayer: “While they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, ‘Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.’ Then after fasting and praying they laid their hands on them and sent them off.” The great missionary journeys of the Church begin with worship, fasting and the laying on of hands. The Psalm is the song of that mission: “All the ends of the earth have seen the victory of our God.”

The Gospel is part of the instructions Jesus gave the Twelve when he sent them out for the first time. “As you go, proclaim the good news, ‘The kingdom of heaven has come near.’ Cure the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, cast out demons.” And then a principle for every missionary: “You received without payment; give without payment.” The apostle travels light, with no gold or silver or copper in his belt, trusting that “laborers deserve their food.” He brings peace into every house he enters: “If the house is worthy, let your peace come upon it.” Barnabas lived this. He gave away his field before he gave away his life. He was big enough to step aside so that Saul, the more gifted preacher, could shine; Acts soon begins to say “Paul and Barnabas” instead of “Barnabas and Saul.” And when Paul refused to take John Mark on a second journey because the young man had left them once before, Barnabas, his cousin, took Mark with him to Cyprus and gave him a second chance (Acts 15:37–39). Years later Paul himself wrote that Mark was useful to him in his ministry (2 Timothy 4:11). The son of encouragement had been right. Tradition says that Barnabas preached in Cyprus and died a martyr at Salamis; the Church of Cyprus honours him as its founder. Every parish needs a Barnabas: someone who sees the grace of God in others and rejoices, who brings the newcomer in, who gives the one who failed a second chance.
outline: Ask: who believed in you when others doubted you, and what difference did it make?

Today say a sincere word of encouragement to someone who is struggling or doubting themselves.

saints: Joseph, a Levite from Cyprus, was named Barnabas, son of encouragement, by the apostles; he sold a field and gave the money to the community (Acts 4:36–37). He introduced the converted Saul to the apostles (Acts 9:27), was sent by the Jerusalem church to Antioch, brought Saul there, and with him was set apart by the Holy Spirit for the first missionary journey, through Cyprus and Asia Minor (Acts 13–14). He took part in the Council of Jerusalem (Acts 15). After parting from Paul over John Mark, his cousin (Colossians 4:10), he sailed with Mark to Cyprus (Acts 15:39). Acts calls him an apostle (Acts 14:14), though he was not one of the Twelve. Tradition holds that he was martyred at Salamis in Cyprus; the Church of Cyprus venerates him as its founder.
2027-06-11.prayer: Lord God, you chose St Barnabas, a good man full of the Holy Spirit and of faith, to strengthen your Church and to carry the Gospel to the nations. Give us his eyes, to see your grace in others and rejoice; his humility, to make room for gifts greater than our own; and his generous heart, to give without payment what we have received without payment. Bless all missionaries, especially those sent from India to other lands, and make us all sons and daughters of encouragement. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: In the Church at Antioch Barnabas and Saul were set apart while the community was “worshiping the Lord and fasting.” The Greek word for worship there is the root of our word liturgy. The mission of the Church is born at the altar. At the end of every Mass we too are sent: Go forth, the Mass is ended; go and announce the Gospel of the Lord. Like Barnabas, we leave the altar to bring Christ's peace into every house we enter.

quick: Barnabas, the son of encouragement, saw the grace of God at Antioch and rejoiced; he was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith.
He went to Tarsus to bring Saul to Antioch, where the disciples were first called Christians; later the Spirit set the two apart for mission.
Jesus sends his apostles to proclaim the kingdom, heal and bring peace: you received without payment; give without payment.
2027-06-11.action: Write or say a word of encouragement today to someone who is new, struggling or has failed.
2027-06-11.question: Do I see the grace of God in others and rejoice, or do I look first for their faults?
kidsaint: Barnabas was a kind man from the island of Cyprus. His real name was Joseph, but the apostles called him Barnabas, which means son of encouragement, because he always cheered people up. When Saul, who used to hurt Christians, became a follower of Jesus, everybody was afraid of him. But Barnabas took him by the hand and said: he has really changed; give him a chance. Saul became the great St Paul! Later Barnabas also gave a young man called Mark a second chance, and Mark wrote one of the four Gospels. Lesson: be an encourager; a kind word can help someone become a saint.

family.explain: The Church in Jerusalem sent Barnabas to the city of Antioch to see what was happening there. He saw that many people had come to believe in Jesus, and he was very happy. He encouraged them. Then he went to find his friend Saul to help him teach. In Antioch the followers of Jesus were first called Christians. That is our name too!
family.intention: We pray for missionaries, for new Christians and for people who need someone to believe in them.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our family or class needs a word of encouragement this week? What will we say to them?”

illus: A young man from a parish in Ernakulam failed his final examinations and stopped coming to church because he was ashamed. Most people forgot him. One elderly member of the parish council, a retired schoolmaster, did not. Every week he stopped by the young man's house with a newspaper cutting about a course or a job, and every week he said: I am praying for you; you are not finished. The young man passed the next year, later trained as a nurse, and now works in a hospital in another state, where he organises the youth group of his parish. When he came home for Christmas he went straight to the old man's house first. The parish priest called the schoolmaster our Barnabas. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Holy Spirit, who set apart Barnabas and Saul for your work, fill us with faith and goodness, and make us encouragers of our brothers and sisters. Amen.
share: When he came and saw the grace of God, he rejoiced (Acts 11:23). When I meet others, do I look first for the grace of God in them?
Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul (Acts 11:25). Is there someone whose gifts I should bring forward, even if they outshine mine?
You received without payment; give without payment (Matthew 10:8). What have I received from God that I am keeping to myself?
pm.resp: The Lord has revealed to the nations his saving power.
interc: For the Church, that she may have many sons and daughters of encouragement who rejoice in the grace of God.
For missionaries, priests, religious and lay people, sent out from Kerala and India to other lands.
For new Christians and those returning to the faith, that they may find a Barnabas who welcomes them.
For the Church in Cyprus and in all the lands where Barnabas preached, and for peace in the Middle East.
For our group, that we may give second chances as Barnabas gave one to Mark.
pm.close: Lord Jesus, you sent your apostles to proclaim that the kingdom has come near. Send us too, with your peace, into every home we enter. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today we celebrate St Barnabas. His real name was Joseph, but the apostles gave him a nickname: Barnabas, son of encouragement (Acts 4:36). Imagine being known in the whole Church for one thing: you make people stronger. What a beautiful reputation!

Look at what he did at Antioch. Something new was happening there: Greeks, not only Jews, were coming to believe in Jesus. Some people in Jerusalem may have been worried. Barnabas came, and when he saw the grace of God, he rejoiced (Acts 11:23). He did not look first for problems. He looked first for grace. Then he encouraged them to remain faithful. That is the first lesson of Barnabas: look for the good God is doing in others, and rejoice in it.

The second lesson is humility. The work at Antioch grew too big for Barnabas, so he went to Tarsus to look for Saul and brought him to Antioch (Acts 11:25–26). He knew Saul was a brilliant teacher, maybe more gifted than himself. He did not mind. Soon everyone was speaking of Paul and Barnabas, not Barnabas and Paul. Later, when Paul did not want to take young Mark on a journey because Mark had once left them, Barnabas gave Mark a second chance. That Mark became a great helper of the Church.

In the Gospel Jesus says to his apostles: you received without payment; give without payment (Matthew 10:8). Barnabas gave his field, his time, his trust, and finally, tradition says, his life in Cyprus. Today let us ask him for a heart like his. Let us look for the grace of God in others, make room for their gifts, give second chances, and be sons and daughters of encouragement. Amen.
kids: Children, do you know what an encourager is? It is someone who says: you can do it! Don't give up! St Barnabas was the best encourager in the Bible. When nobody trusted Saul, Barnabas trusted him, and Saul became St Paul. When young Mark made a mistake, Barnabas gave him another chance, and Mark wrote a Gospel! Today, say an encouraging word to a friend. You might be helping a future saint!
